title: Attrition of sexual offences in police investigations
abstract: The attrition of reported sexual violence offences is an ongoing issue in Australia, with more than 40 percent of offences being withdrawn by the victim-survivor or labelled by investigators as unfounded. Factors that can influence case outcomes include offence characteristics, police responses to sexual offences, resource availability and system-level barriers. We use a mixed-methods design to evaluate the case, police and system factors that influence withdrawn and unfounded case outcomes for sexual offences in Queensland. We analyse administrative Queensland Police Service data on sexual offences from 2017 to 2022 and outcomes of interviews and focus groups with police and service providers in Queensland. We find that high demand, limited capacity and increased sexual offence severity are increasing withdrawn and unfounded outcomes. Specialist sexual offence trained investigators and referrals to external services are the most consistent protective factors against withdrawn and unfounded case outcomes.
